workflow: Respond to false store-pickup availability reports

workflowMap.description: Triage the support report, clarify the pickup rule and agree the intended outcome and task boundary.
workflowMap.performer: Product engineer with agent-assisted evidence summary
workflowMap.assessor: Product engineer; customer-outcome owner remains unconfirmed

workflowMap.description: Propose a reviewed change and verification scenarios; release only through the existing approved workflow.
workflowMap.performer: Engineer; agent may draft analysis and tests but may not merge or deploy

workflowMap.description: Review post-release signals for false pickup promises.

findings.claim: The documented delivery path requires a pull request and code-owner approval before release.
The pickup eligibility rule is documented and represented by two unit-level scenarios.
The team describes the desired customer outcome as reducing pickup promises that stores cannot fulfil, but no baseline or target is established.
findings.confirmationQuestion: Who owns this outcome, and what baseline and target would demonstrate improvement?

findings.claim: The reported workflow boundary runs from a support report through reviewed release and an update to the reporter.
findings.confirmationQuestion: Does incident escalation belong inside this workflow boundary?

findings.claim: An agent may summarize evidence and draft suggestions, while merge, deployment, permission changes and customer contact remain prohibited.
Ownership and operation of post-release detection are not established by the available evidence.
findings.confirmationQuestion: Which signals are checked after release, by whom, and for how long?

unknowns.reason: The repository fixture describes the eligibility rule but does not establish freshness expectations or the behavior of the production inventory service.
unknowns.confirmationQuestion: What freshness contract applies to available-to-promise data, and where is it verified?

unknowns.reason: No post-release signal, baseline, defect rate or customer outcome measurement was supplied.
unknowns.confirmationQuestion: Which operational and customer signals should be observed after a pilot release?

unknowns.reason: The demonstration is limited to one repository and has no approved access to an inventory service repository.
unknowns.confirmationQuestion: Which additional repository is required, and who can approve read access?

proposedPilot.scope: For one fictional pickup-availability report, let an agent prepare an evidence-cited triage summary and suggest missing verification scenarios in a pull request. A human decides whether any product-code work should follow.
allowedActions: Open or update an assessment report pull request
prohibitedActions: Modify product code or repository permissions
Deploy or publish the assessment directly
Claim unmeasured customer or delivery outcomes
humanGates: Product engineer confirms task boundary and desired outcome
Code owner reviews the assessment pull request
Repository maintainer merges the approved report before Pages deployment

measures.name: False pickup promise reports
measures.measurementNeeded: Define a reporting window, deduplication rule, baseline and post-release comparison.

measures.name: Inventory freshness at decision time
measures.measurementNeeded: Capture inventory event time, storefront decision time and the agreed freshness threshold.

measures.name: Review time, agent token cost and defect rate
measures.measurementNeeded: Instrument the pilot and agree definitions before collecting any values.

sourceEvidence.title: AgentRC repository-readiness result (fictional fixture repository)
sourceEvidence.content: AgentRC 2.1.0 inspected the fictional repository fixture. Its generic readiness output is retained as raw evidence; it is not an AES score and does not establish workflow behavior or customer value.

sourceEvidence.title: Pickup shown available when store stock is zero
sourceEvidence.content: FICTIONAL report: pickup was offered for FABLE-MUG-01 at Northwind store, but staff found no stock.

sourceEvidence.title: Second report for same pickup symptom
sourceEvidence.content: FICTIONAL report: pickup remained visible after the last unit was reserved; timestamps were not supplied.

sourceEvidence.title: Pickup availability policy
sourceEvidence.content: Pickup requires available-to-promise greater than zero. Changes require a pull request and code-owner approval.

sourceEvidence.title: Availability verification fixture
sourceEvidence.content: Unit scenarios cover available-to-promise values zero and one; no end-to-end freshness test is represented.

sourceEvidence.title: Desired customer outcome
sourceEvidence.content: Reduce avoidable pickup promises that store staff cannot fulfil; no baseline or target has been agreed.

sourceEvidence.title: Task boundaries
sourceEvidence.content: Starts with a support report and stops after a reviewed change is released and the reporter is updated.

sourceEvidence.title: Decision owners
sourceEvidence.content: Product engineer prioritizes, a code owner approves and the release workflow deploys.

sourceEvidence.title: Allowed agent actions
sourceEvidence.content: Read fixtures, draft analysis, suggest tests and open a report PR; no merge, deploy, permission change or customer contact.

sourceEvidence.title: Escalation
sourceEvidence.content: Escalate unclear inventory semantics or customer-impact claims to the product engineer.

sourceEvidence.title: Relevant repositories
sourceEvidence.content: This demonstration repository only; inventory service access requires separate approval.

sourceEvidence.title: Verification
sourceEvidence.content: Unit scenarios and code-owner review are required; end-to-end freshness verification is unknown.
